item.title: Cape Town Developer User Group Meetup
item.description:
The meetup with a view - Cape Town Developer User Group.

Have you ever had a meetup with the perfect view of the Atlantic Ocean. Speaking next to where you board the ferry to the history filled Robben Island. Yeah, I never thought I would, but I did. And afterwards, took a boat to Robben Island for the History.

Session: Building AI Solutions in Azure AI Foundry

For this meetup, I went with if it is not broke it needs no fixing and redelivered the same session I did in Joburg. Difference, I got so many questions, much more interaction with the Audince and as a plus, got to hear my collegues sessions as well.

item.title: Microsoft AI Tour Johannesburg
item.description:
The city of the hustle and bustle - AI Tour Joburg.

Last week I missed a post, I know. I spent the week confused, hurt and betrayed. One day I will look back but I was on my lows. So this week, we do two event recaps anddddd…. some lessons I picked from the Robben Island, reading a new book, Busy Idiots and just existing.

Okay, let’s get to the meat of it all. This week I arrived in South Africa early Tuesday mid-morning, ready to work, tour and prepared for the week ahead. And for the first time, I was here for just that one breakout session, and spending time with colleagues.

item.title: Microsoft AI Tour Bengaluru
item.description:
💡 First speaking engagement 2025 in Bengaluru, India

It’s been a while since I’ve written an event recap — surprising, considering I spend so much time attending and speaking at conferences! Events are at the core of DevRel, where learning, sharing, and connecting happen in real-time. So, I’ve decided to make it a tradition: documenting my speaking engagements not only as a personal reflection but also as a resource for anyone interested in the topics I cover.

item.title: What if perfection is in completion?
item.description:
💡 What if the only way to achieve perfection is completing your own damn work?

For the longest time, I’ve been staring at blank pages. The idea of perfection in my head seems impossible to achieve in real life, leaving me frozen, unable to start. Time and again, I find myself struggling to take that first step.

My process always starts with endless planning. It begins with a spark—something lights up in my brain, like my idea for a newsletter. Then I create list after list: topics I want to cover, actions needed to bring the idea to life. Gradually, I designed the whole newsletter layout. Yet a year later, all I have is a Substack page with nothing but a “launching soon” sign.

item.title: Learnings on Money
item.description: I am no expert when it comes to finances but I’ve been doing this long enough that my friends believe I can share some nuggets. To start of, the main and greatest lesson I have learnt is personal finance is personal. Although you may have similiarities with your family, neighbours or even friends, when it comes to money - experiences are unique and varied.
